hints.title: Reverse Boundary Flood
hints.text: Instead of finding enclaves directly, eliminate all land cells that can walk off the grid boundary. These are exactly the land cells connected to the outer perimeter.

hints.title: Border Seeding
hints.text: Initiate depth-first or breadth-first traversals starting from every land cell located on the top, bottom, left, and right outer edges of the grid.

hints.title: Remaining Land Summation
hints.text: As boundary components are traversed, overwrite their land cells with 0. Once all boundary-connected land is cleared, simply count the remaining 1 cells across the matrix.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Traversing from each individual land cell independently risks revisiting nodes multiple times, causing O((M*N)^2) behavior.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Boundary flood fill visits each cell at most once, running in linear time relative to grid size.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize that boundary-connected components can be flooded first to leave only enclosed enclaves.
complexity.notes: Can also be solved using Disjoint Set Union by uniting border cells to a dummy boundary node.
